# NitroCore runtime hash lock -- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.
#
# Source file: NitroCore/requirements.txt (exact pins; this lock is
# the full resolved set -- both pins are direct, neither has
# transitive dependencies).
# Install with:  pip install --require-hashes -r NitroCore/requirements.lock.txt
# Any hash mismatch or unlisted package FAILS the install. That is
# the point: owner policy 2026-10-25 (--require-hashes fleet
# rollout) -- a version bump is not landed until its hashes are
# locked here.
#
# Generated: 2026-10-25, hashes ONLY from downloaded index
# artifacts (`pip download` + `pip hash`, pip 26.2.2):
#   pip download --no-deps --platform win_amd64 --only-binary=:all:
#       --python-version <39|310|311|312|313> pywin32==312
#   pip download --no-deps --platform win_amd64 --only-binary=:all:
#       psutil==7.0.0
#   pip download --no-deps psutil==7.0.0            (manylinux wheel)
#   pip download --no-deps --no-binary=:all: psutil==7.0.0  (sdist)
#   pip hash <each downloaded artifact>
# pywin32 ships no sdist on PyPI that pip can use and no
# non-Windows wheels at all; `pip download --no-binary=:all:
# pywin32==312` returns "No matching distribution found" (observed
# 2026-10-25) -- its entries below are wheel hashes only, which is
# what a Windows install consumes.
#
# Platform coverage: Windows win_amd64, CPython 3.9-3.13 (the
# pywin32 wheels are per-interpreter; psutil's win_amd64 wheel is
# one cp37-abi3 file covering all of them). pywin32 carries the
# same sys_platform == "win32" marker pyproject.toml gives it, so
# on Linux this lock installs psutil only -- that is exactly what
# the Linux clean-install proof proves (psutil's manylinux wheel +
# sdist hashes below), and NO Linux install of pywin32 is claimed:
# none exists. The 32-bit win32 and win_arm64 pywin32 wheels are
# NOT in this lock; CI and release runners are win_amd64.
#
# Regeneration: re-run the downloads above for the pins in
# requirements.txt, re-hash, then re-run the clean-venv install
# proof and the tamper test before committing. NEVER hand-copy a
# hash from anywhere but a downloaded index artifact.
#
# Build-system note (bounded exception): pyproject.toml pins
# setuptools==84.1.0 as its build requirement. pip's build
# isolation cannot hash-check build dependencies, so `pip
# install .` fetches that one already-exact pin unverified by
# hash. Mitigation: install the dev or release lock first (both
# contain setuptools==84.1.0 with hashes) and build with
# --no-build-isolation; the pin itself is unchanged.
